claimRules: "Needs no supervisor" does not mean simpler, cheaper or more reliable. Each of those is a separate claim that needs its own evidence, or it is not made.
A result that holds only at one setting of the rival's assumptions is stated with that setting, never as a general claim.
A claim about locality names its failure model: per crash or per process (`bench/PREREG.md` §6).
The fairness rules (`bench/REPORT.md` §1) are never revisited to rescue a result.
Replay proves that this code produces the recorded run from the recorded model outputs. It does not prove where those outputs came from. Say exactly that.

M1.text: In the recorded demo run, 65% of input tokens were served from cache.

R1.text: Recovery stays local to the affected subtree.

R2.status: allowed (gate, Oct 29; real rows, Oct 30, re-read at ten seeds)
R2.text: Resilience comparable to an ideal durable supervisor, without a central coordinator or a separate recovery mechanism.

R3.text: The conditions: against the ideal durable supervisor on the conference task, with five coordinator crashes and half the agents killed, locality holds when the supervisor needs 1–3 s more to restart a coordinator (coordinator-dependency time 0.28 and 0.19 of the supervisor's); it ties at the default assumptions (both detect a failure in 5 s, no extra restart) and when both detect in 1–10 s; it fails when an external supervisor detects and restarts within 0.5–1 s while the swarm keeps its 5 s detection (13.2 and 5.7 times the supervisor's). Per process, each coordinator process failing at the same rate, the two are comparable (ratio 0.90), and the supervisor recovers sooner. The swarm's failure detector also produces false deaths (1.25–2.25 per run at three and five crashes), the supervisors none.

R4.status: allowed with its setting (Oct 30, re-read at ten seeds)
R4.text: On the real model, at the headline point (T2, C3: five coordinator crashes, half the agents killed), locality against the ideal durable supervisor tied over ten seeds: the swarm's coordinator-dependency time, blast radius and idle agent-seconds were 0.57, 0.43 and 0.70 of its values, and at or below half on 4, 7 and 6 of the ten seeds.

R5.status: allowed with its setting (Oct 30, re-read at ten seeds)
R5.text: Against an in-process supervisor, whose workers die with it, the swarm at C3 stalled 11.2 s against 42.8 s, with +2.4% extra cost against +67.0% on the pre-registered basis (which estimates the cost of cancelled calls), or −1.1% against +29.2% on completed calls only.

R6.status: allowed with its link (Oct 30, re-read at ten seeds)
R6.text: On the real model, with five of its ten coordinators crashed and half its agents killed, every run finished with a valid result. It stalled 11.2 s against 42.8 s for an in-process supervisor, and tied an ideal durable supervisor on stall time and extra cost.

R7.text: Per crash, on the real model, at the headline point (T2, C3: five coordinator crashes, half the agents killed), against a realistic durable supervisor, which loses its own in-flight plan and judge calls and redoes them after the restart, the swarm's coordinator-dependency time was 11.4 s against 50.3 s and a crash held up 9.0% of the sessions against 37.3%, at or below half on each of the ten seeds.

S1.text: No separate recovery mechanism: every survivor computes the same heir from the log with one rule (HRW), so there is no election.

S2.text: Any orchestrator can die mid-run, the root included, and the run still finishes.

S3.text: No process manager, standby or election service.

S4.status: allowed as a property of the design, never as an advantage over the rivals
S4.text: Zero LLM tokens spent on coordination.

S5.text: Every run replays bit-for-bit from a hash-verified log; `fractalswarm demo --verify` needs no API key.

S7.status: allowed. The measured numbers go under it as a subtitle, each with its rival named (R2, R3), never as part of the tagline
S7.text: The tagline: "Kill half the brains. It still finishes." Only that sentence (Yoel, Oct 30).
